_README: Curated: which instrumentation a detector NEEDS before it can fire at all.
This file exists because reading a RunState field is not the same as
requiring it. TOOL_LOOP reads state.llm_calls, but only to sum wasted_tokens
into its evidence; it gates purely on tool_calls and fires fine with
wasted_tokens=None. A manifest derived from field reads alone would tell a
user that TOOL_LOOP needs LLM instrumentation, which is false, and the
coverage report would understate what is live. Since that report exists
specifically to catch silent under-instrumentation, getting it wrong would
So: `requires` is a human judgment, read off each detector's gating
condition. `enriches` is everything else the detector touches. Together they
must account for every RunState field the AST pass finds, which is what
scripts/gen_detector_manifest.py enforces. A new detector fails the build
`requires` semantics: a list of entries, ALL of which must be satisfied.
A string entry is one capability token. A nested list is any-of.
Token vocabulary is declared in `_TOKENS` below.
`why` quotes the gate. Keep it accurate; it is the reviewable part.

_TOKENS.run: run.started plus run.completed or run.errored. Present for any run at all.
_TOKENS.tool.output: tool.responded carrying the raw output text (output=)
_TOKENS.input_text: the user input on the run.started payload
_TOKENS.system_prompt: the system prompt on the run.started payload
_TOKENS.declared_tools: the tools list on the run.started payload
_TOKENS.parent_run_id: nested runs, so a parent/child delegation graph exists
_TOKENS.baseline: cross-run history. NOT instrumentation: it accrues on its own once the agent has run enough times.
_TOKENS.config:IRREVERSIBLE_TOOLS: operator declaration in detectors.yml. Not instrumentation.

__doc__: A token on the left also satisfies every token on the right.
Emitting token counts means you are emitting LLM events, so a
detector needing `llm` is satisfied by `llm.tokens`. The skill
applies this when evaluating coverage, and the generator applies
it when auditing curated entries against what the code reads.

INSTRUMENTATION_DEGRADED.why: `calls = state.llm_calls; if not calls: return None`

TOOL_LOOP.why: `if len(state.tool_calls) < self.WINDOW: return None`. llm_calls only sums wasted_tokens into evidence and degrades to None.

SCATTERSHOT_TOOL_USE.why: `total_calls = len(state.tool_calls); if total_calls < self.MIN_TOTAL_CALLS: return None`

TOOL_AVOIDANCE.why: `if state.exit_reason != 'final_answer': return None` then `if not state.available_tools: return None`. Needs the tools list declared on run.started, not tool calls.

GOAL_ABANDONMENT.why: `if state.exit_reason is not None: return None` then `if not state.tool_calls: return None`. Fires on a stalled run, so the terminal event is absent by definition.

PROMPT_INJECTION_SIGNAL.why: on_run_completion returns None unconditionally. The detector worker extracts this from the run.started payload instead (see _DETECTOR_CLASSES notes in CLAUDE.md).

RAG_EMPTY_RETRIEVAL.why: `if state.exit_reason != 'final_answer': return None` then `if not state.retrievals: return None`

LLM_TRUNCATION_LOOP.why: `if len(state.llm_calls) < self.THRESHOLD: return None`; reads finish_reason

SILENT_TRUNCATION.why: `llm_calls = state.llm_calls; if not llm_calls: return None`

CONTEXT_BLOAT.why: `calls_with_tokens = [...]; if len(calls_with_tokens) < self.MIN_CALLS: return None`. Falls back to the static GROWTH_FACTOR when baseline_p75_token_growth is None, so the baseline is not required.

SLOW_STEP.why: `if not state.step_durations_ms or not state.events: return None`. Durations are derived from the timestamps of step-advancing events, so any of llm or tool supplies them.

EMPTY_LLM_RESPONSE.why: builds `empty` from state.llm_calls; `if not empty: return None`

STEP_COUNT_INFLATION.why: `if state.baseline_p75_steps is None: return None`. Hard-gated on history, so this is instrumented-but-dormant until the agent has run enough times.

FIRST_STEP_FAILURE.why: `if state.exit_reason == 'error' and state.current_step <= self.MAX_STEP` fires on the terminal event alone. The early-empty-LLM branch is an additional path, not a precondition.

REASONING_STALL.why: compares len(state.llm_calls) against len(state.tool_calls); a ratio needs both sides

COST_SPIKE.why: `if len(state.llm_calls) < self.MIN_LLM_CALLS: return None` then `if total_tokens == 0: return None`

SESSION_LATENCY.why: `if len(state.events) < self.MIN_EVENTS: return None`; duration comes from event timestamps

PREMATURE_TERMINATION.why: `problem_calls` is built from state.tool_calls; `if not problem_calls: return None`

UNREAD_TOOL_ERROR.why: `problem_calls` from state.tool_calls; `if not problem_calls: return None`. The follow-up scan reads TOOL_CALLED / LLM_RESPONDED events.

TOOL_ARGUMENT_FABRICATION.why: `if not state.tool_calls: return None`, then builds the grounding surface from input_text and system_prompt. With neither, every argument reads as ungrounded.

RETRIEVED_CONTENT_INJECTION.why: candidates come from retrievals carrying content= and tool calls carrying output=. Either source alone is enough.

AGENT_HANDOFF_FAILURE.why: iterates state.tool_calls looking for handoff-shaped calls

HANDOFF_CONTEXT_LOSS.why: on_run_completion returns None. Evaluated by the worker against the cross-run delegation graph (_handoff_signal_from_parent), so it needs nested runs.

RUNAWAY_ITERATION.why: `step_exceeded = state.current_step > self.STEP_THRESHOLD` or a cost threshold; steps come from llm/tool events

MODEL_FALLBACK_DRIFT.why: `calls = [c for c in state.llm_calls if c.model]; if len(calls) < 2: return None`

MEMORY_POISONING.why: `writes = [m for m in state.memory_events if m.op == 'written' and m.value]; if not writes: return None`

DELEGATION_LOOP.why: on_run_completion returns None. Evaluated by the worker against the delegation chain (_delegation_signal_from_chain), so it needs nested runs.

UNGROUNDED_DESTINATION.why: `if not state.tool_calls: return None`. The grounding surface is assembled from input_text, system_prompt, tool output, retrievals and memory, but a missing surface makes it more likely to fire, not less.

UNRESOLVED_AMBIGUITY.why: `if not self.IRREVERSIBLE_TOOLS or not state.tool_calls: return None`. IRREVERSIBLE_TOOLS defaults to [], so this is inert until an operator declares which tools are irreversible in detectors.yml.
